A.notes: Strong scroll idea tied to the brief: bold hero, oversized date transition, then a scrubbed/pinned line-up reveal that counts through all 18 artists before moving to stages/tickets. Consecutive desktop frames show a coherent progression rather than isolated fades. Mobile keeps the same idea, but the narrow viewport makes the line-up motion feel cramped: several cards are clipped mid-entry/mid-exit, and some frames show awkward partial reveals that hurt legibility. Reduced-motion is clearly reworked: much shorter page, line-up becomes a readable static grid, and the content does not depend on animation. Craft is mixed: no blank states, but there are repeated half-revealed cards and edge clipping, especially on mobile. Stills cannot confirm easing/timing quality.

B.notes: The motion idea appears lighter and more conventional. Frames suggest mostly vertical section-to-section progression with some headline swaps/scale changes and a card-catalogue reveal, but not a strong festival-specific scroll mechanic. The sequence is coherent and readable, yet less authored than Site A: fewer clear pinned or scrubbed moments are evident from the strip. Mobile holds together well; the simpler motion survives the small viewport without obvious clipping or broken transitions. Reduced-motion appears almost identical to full-motion, which suggests limited adaptation, but all content remains readable and does not seem to rely on motion to make sense. Craft is clean from the strips: no blank frames, no overlap failures, no obvious half-stuck elements. Stills cannot confirm easing/timing or any subtle background animation.
